originalFailure: A current-source full closeout authorization was validated, but selectCiPlan ignored it when the actual diff did not require full audit. releasePreflight correctly rejected the resulting selected-only PR plan.
rootCause: Plan scope depended exclusively on selectTests.status. Full-tests authorization was only used to permit a broad diff, never to express the already-approved complete release test intent for a narrow or evidence-only diff.
whyEarlierCoverageMissedIt: Earlier real preflight fixtures used a broad historical PR base and expected the narrow push to remain selected. A separate assertion incorrectly treated a narrow PR with valid full-tests authorization as an intentional blocker. Current-main closeout bases exposed that contradictory policy before push.
fix: The only production change makes a successfully validated supplied authorization also select the full inventory; any supplied sourceDigest mismatch still fails. buildCiPlan trust and releaseAuthorization validation, runCi full-inventory revalidation and production releasePreflight full-plan assertion remain unchanged.
preservedBoundaries: No new mode, environment bypass, false historical base, source authorization, audit record, timeout, concurrency setting or test retry was introduced.
Unapproved PR files cannot authenticate themselves; narrow unapproved PRs stay selected, evidence-only unapproved PRs stay no-behavior-change, and broad unapproved changes are rejected.
Explicit wrong checksums, missing authorization files, source drift, insufficient full-tests scope and an unintegrated target base remain blockers.
The existing trusted main/manual/externally approved PR distinction and stale PR repository-variable isolation remain unchanged.
A release preflight still checks committed source and committed authorization bytes, exact head/ancestor, pinned tools and real build artifacts; it does not claim tests or release gate success.

redRegression.source: New regression assertions executed against unchanged original production planner before applying the one-line behavior fix.

failures.name: build metadata requires explicit current-source authorization, never an implicit full run
a trusted full closeout selects the whole inventory for a narrow diff
a trusted full closeout selects the whole inventory for a evidence-only diff
preflight binds two actual plans and reusable build outputs without executing tests

skippedCases.name: root fixtures have a traversable disposable temp outside their private home

windows.prerequisites: Unified task-local launcher supplies pinned Node 24.22.1, explicit verified Python, official CLI and Go manifest; one existing POSIX-only filesystem-mode case is recorded as skipped on Windows.

linux.method: Independent isolated ordinary-user checkout using pinned Node 24.22.1, explicit /usr/bin/python3 and actual runVitest/isolateTestProcess. Re-read all six returned artifacts, compared all 72 case identities and verified every current public source file hash against the transferred manifest.

limits: These are targeted tooling tests, not a full-suite run or a completed release gate.
Real Git-backed releasePreflight regressions use intentionally tiny offline build executables to validate orchestration, artifact binding and reuse, not TS/Vite production compilation.
The working release candidate must receive a new audit/source-bound authorization and committed-head preflight after this source change; no stale candidate authorization was refreshed here.
Original preflight refusal and original Hosted/local failures remain failures; the fix does not relabel them as successful.
